title: Cadence — Chord Progression Workbench
description: Build progressions in any key and mode, let the voice-leading engine pick the voicings, then export a real .mid file.
concept: A songwriting workbench rather than a keyboard toy. Pick one of 12 roots and 9 modes, stack diatonic chords plus fourteen borrowed and secondary options, and Cadence re-harmonises everything in place when you change key. A voice-leading solver searches every inversion and register to find the voicing closest to the chord before it, a Markov table suggests where the ear wants to go next, and the whole thing plays back through four synthesised instruments with swing, bass and convolution room. Export the result as a two-track Standard MIDI File, an offline-rendered WAV, pattern JSON or a shareable link.
features: 12 roots x 9 modes with live re-harmonisation of the existing progression
Diatonic palette plus 14 borrowed/secondary chords, six chord colours (triad, 7th, 9th, 6th, sus4, add9)
Voice-leading solver that minimises semitone movement across inversions and registers
Markov next-chord suggestion panel with probability bars, plus a weighted random generator
Four synthesised instruments, four playback patterns, swing, bass line, metronome and convolution reverb
Animated piano-roll of the actual voicings with a live playhead
Export: Standard MIDI File (.mid, 2 tracks), offline-rendered WAV, pattern JSON, shareable URL hash
12 starter progressions and localStorage save slots

interaction.mouse: Click a numeral to append a chord; click a slot to select it and reveal its beats / colour / octave controls.
interaction.click: Play loops the progression; export buttons write .mid, .wav and .json straight to disk.
interaction.touch: Tap chords and slots, drag the sliders, swipe the progression strip sideways.
interaction.keyboard: Space plays, 1-7 add diatonic chords (shift for 7ths), arrows select, backspace deletes, c clears.
